items.title: Beyond VLAs: How World Action Models Reshape Robot Manipulation
items.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) build on video world models instead of vision-language models (VLMs), enabling robot policies with stronger physical generalization. A strong foundation for post-training WAMs is the open NVIDIA Cosmos 3 model, which provides practical deployment at multiple tiers and measurable improvements in policy performance. Unlike VLA models, WAMs learn from diverse data and generalize in the open world, adapting to new robots with few demonstrations.
items.audio_script: From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Beyond VLAs: How World Action Models Reshape Robot Manipulation," this story explores how World Action Models (WAMs) build upon video world models instead of vision-language models, resulting in robot policies with stronger physical generalization. According to the recent advancements reported, researchers at NVIDIA have developed a new approach that leverages the open NVIDIA Cosmos 3 model as a strong foundation for post-training WAMs, enabling practical deployment at multiple tiers and measuring significant improvements in policy performance. This approach differs from existing models, such as VLA models, which learn from diverse data and generalize in the open world, adapting to new robots with minimal demonstrations. By extending this concept to robotics, WAMs offer a promising solution for improving robot manipulation capabilities.

items.title: Bridging the Gap Between Robotics Design and Deployment
items.summary: Laboratories can only simulate certain aspects of real-world environments, making it challenging for robots to be resilient and predictable in deployment. Early field testing helps identify flaws early in design, speeding up the design feedback loop cycle. Building a strong robotics deployment pipeline requires iterating development on platforms and designing technology that people will trust, including factors like signaling intentions and safety points. The role of the feedback loop in deployment involves using real data to optimize performance and strengthen design autonomy through iteration-based innovation.
items.audio_script:
From Robotics & Automation News, "Bridging the Gap Between Robotics Design and Deployment", researchers have made significant strides in bridging the gap between robotics design and deployment by utilizing early field testing to identify flaws and speed up the design feedback loop cycle. This process involves simulating real-world environments in laboratories, which, while able to mimic certain aspects, fall short of replicating the complexities and unpredictability of actual settings. To overcome this limitation, developers are focusing on building strong robotics deployment pipelines that prioritize iteration-based innovation, signaling intentions, and safety protocols.

Early field testing has proven instrumental in identifying design flaws early on, allowing for swift adjustments and refinements to be made before robots enter production. By leveraging real-world data, researchers can optimize performance and strengthen design autonomy through iterative innovation. This approach enables the development of more resilient and predictable robots that can thrive in a variety of environments.

The success of this methodology has significant implications for the AI/tech industry, as it sets the stage for more efficient and effective deployment of robotics technology. As developers continue to refine their approaches, it will be exciting to see how these advancements impact industries such as manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, where robots are increasingly being integrated into workflows.

items.title: Zoox unveils production-ready robotaxi for U.S. expansion
items.summary: Zoox has unveiled the final production design of its robotaxi, featuring a new color scheme and improved rider comfort features such as screens, controls, and drink holders. The vehicle's cabin has been designed to be "carriage-like" with no steering wheel or pedals, seating four adult passengers facing each other. The updated materials are built to withstand urban wear and tear while offering higher contrast for easier spotting of personal items. Zoox plans to produce 100 vehicles per week at its new manufacturing facility in Hayward, California, as it prepares for full approval from the NHTSA.

The vehicle's cabin has been designed to resemble a carriage with no steering wheel or pedals, accommodating four adult passengers facing each other. The updated materials are built to withstand urban wear and tear while offering higher contrast for easier spotting of personal items. According to Zoox, the company plans to produce 100 vehicles per week at its new manufacturing facility in Hayward, California, as it awaits full approval from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

items.title: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super, the Frontier Open Model for Robotaxis and Autonomous Vehicles, Now Available for Commercial Use
items.summary: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super is now available for commercial use, offering advanced reasoning capabilities for robotaxis and autonomous vehicles. Built on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Super Reasoner and post-trained with reinforcement learning, the model advances the AV ecosystem with leading multitask capabilities and open commercial licensing. The model ranks first on LingoQA and other benchmarks, demonstrating state-of-the-art reasoning for driving-centric scenarios.

items.title: Beyond the Viral Demo: Sunday Robotics Claims 99.1% Zero-Shot Success in Laundry Folding with ACT-2
items.summary: Sunday Robotics introduced ACT-2, a model achieving a 99.1% autonomous success rate in folding laundry across unseen home environments without requiring per-home data collection or expert demonstrations. The system closes the "generalization gap" by scaling pretraining on diverse data and exhibits emergent behaviors such as recovering dropped garments and continuing tasks despite physical disturbances. A new evaluation framework called a "Solve" is proposed, which evaluates tasks based on performance, scope, and adaptation cost rather than isolated demonstrations.
items.audio_script:
From Humanoids Daily, "Beyond the Viral Demo: Sunday Robotics Claims 99.1% Zero-Shot Success in Laundry Folding with ACT-2". This story showcases Sunday Robotics' introduction of a model called ACT-2 that has demonstrated an impressive 99.1% autonomous success rate in folding laundry across unseen home environments.

Sunday Robotics developed ACT-2 by scaling pretraining on diverse data, closing the "generalization gap" and enabling the system to exhibit emergent behaviors such as recovering dropped garments and continuing tasks despite physical disturbances. The approach employed by Sunday Robotics relies on a novel evaluation framework called a "Solve", which assesses task performance, scope, and adaptation cost rather than isolated demonstrations. By adopting this method, ACT-2 achieves exceptional zero-shot success without requiring per-home data collection or expert demonstrations.

The success of ACT-2 marks an important milestone in the field of artificial intelligence, highlighting advancements in robot learning and generalization capabilities. As researchers continue to explore ways to improve AI systems' adaptability and performance, the results from Sunday Robotics' ACT-2 model are poised to have significant implications for future developments.

items.title: Persona AI Humanoids Touch Down in Korea Following Successful Teleoperated Welding Demo
items.summary: Persona AI has deployed humanoids to South Korea for early integration work ahead of its Gen 3 deliveries at the end of the year. The deployment follows a successful teleoperated welding demo by Persona AI's Gen 1 robot in July, which validated its core actuation and kinematics. The company is partnering with HD Hyundai to commercialize humanoid labor for shipyard environments, and the arrival of hardware in Korea aligns closely with this partnership.

items.title: The 1X Neo Robot Has Freaky Fast Fingers | WIRED
items.summary: 1X's Neo robot features soft, helpful hands with actuators designed to replicate human hand movement, providing 25 degrees of freedom and enabling tasks like opening doors, lifting heavy objects, and plugging itself in. The hands have an IP68 waterproof rating and can grip odd shapes, detect slipping, and move extremely quickly. The robot's design is inspired by characters like Baymax, with a focus on being soft, supple, and safe for human interaction. Early access pricing starts at $20,000 or $500 per month, and the robot is currently partly teleoperated, allowing humans to remotely control it in "Expert Mode."

items.title: Qualcomm-powered robot collapses spectacularly on stage during company's keynote — prepared stagehands rush to cloak and then carry off stricken humanoid (updated) | Tom's Hardware
items.summary: A Qualcomm-powered robot called 4NE-1 collapsed spectacularly on stage during a press event at Computex 2026, just seconds into its presentation. The robot's slow shambling walking style was mocked by some, but the real moment of comedy came when it suddenly and noisily crashed to the ground, prompting stagehands to quickly cloak and carry it away. The presenter continued his speech as if nothing had happened, and the audience applauded politely for him, rather than the robot's mishap. The incident has been compared to a Windows 98 software crash event, which may have led to the creation of the infamous "USB Cart of Death".
items.audio_script:
From tomshardware.com, "Qualcomm-powered robot collapses spectacularly on stage during company's keynote — prepared stagehands rush to cloak and then carry off stricken humanoid (updated) | Tom's Hardware". The robot's slow shambling walking style was momentarily mocked by some in attendance, but the real moment of comedy came when it crashed to the ground, prompting prepared stagehands to quickly cloak and carry it away. The presenter continued his speech as if nothing had happened, while the audience applauded politely for him, rather than the robot's mishap.

The incident has been compared to a Windows 98 software crash event, which may have led to the creation of the infamous "USB Cart of Death". The robot's collapse was reportedly due to an unspecified issue with its mechanical legs. In the aftermath, Qualcomm officials have not yet commented on what caused the bot to malfunction or when it will be available for public testing.

The incident serves as a reminder that even the most advanced AI-powered robots can experience technical issues. As such, it's essential to monitor future developments in this area and watch for any potential improvements in robot reliability and safety protocols.

items.title: Cold calling: How autonomous robots are transforming polar science in the Arctic and Antarctic
items.summary: Autonomous robots are transforming polar science in the Arctic and Antarctic by collecting data from remote and inhospitable environments. They operate underwater, on the ocean surface, and in the air, allowing scientists to monitor glaciers, oceans, wildlife, and climate processes over long periods. Autonomous vehicles, such as gliders and drones, can work in places humans cannot, reducing risks and increasing efficiency. Researchers believe artificial intelligence will become increasingly important in coordinating different sources of information, but robots are not expected to replace scientists entirely.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Cold calling: How autonomous robots are transforming polar science in the Arctic and Antarctic," this story highlights how autonomous robots are revolutionizing polar research by collecting data from remote environments. Autonomous vehicles such as gliders and drones have enabled scientists to monitor glaciers, oceans, wildlife, and climate processes over extended periods with reduced risks and increased efficiency. Using advanced sensors and artificial intelligence, these robots can operate underwater, on the ocean surface, and in the air, providing a wealth of information that would be impossible for humans to collect. As AI technology continues to advance, researchers expect it will play an increasingly important role in coordinating data from various sources, while also expanding the capabilities of autonomous vehicles.

items.title: Light-Loco-Parkour: Versatile Perceptive Whole-Body Locomotion via Multi-Skill Distillation
items.summary: LLP, a single deployable policy, enables autonomous perceptive whole-body locomotion on a humanoid in outdoor settings using only onboard sensing. The system acquires terrain-conditioned skills from sparse seeds and learns autonomous skill transitions from reward. LLP outperforms existing humanoid systems by tracking velocity in open terrain, executing whole-body traversal at obstacles, and resuming locomotion afterward, with no reference input or skill label. Simulation and real-world experiments show high success across benchmarked terrains and unseen obstacle variations.

items.title: Semantic Haptic Feedback Enhances Dexterous Robotic Teleoperation
items.summary: Semantic haptic feedback enhances dexterous robotic teleoperation by using abstract patterns to convey critical information about robot states, simplifying hardware requirements and enabling one-to-many mappings. The approach categorizes robot states into "Confirmations" and "Exceptions", implements a modular haptic rendering pipeline in robot simulation, and delivers semantic haptic feedback through pneumatic and vibrotactile wristbands. Three evaluation studies show that semantic haptics performs similarly to other feedback approaches in unimanual tasks but achieves superior performance in bimanual tasks with reduced task workload, increased situational awareness, and overall preference.

items.title: Toward Certified Functional Safety for Industrial Humanoid Robots: The Fail-Passive Gap and a Feasibility Study
items.summary: Industrial humanoid robots face a lack of functional safety certification due to the fail-passive gap, where actively-controlled states on the robot-side violate the assume-safe state assumption. A certified external safety chain is used to locate this issue precisely, pinpointing it to the robot-side reaction chain. The approach involves analyzing the balancing policy and its residual risk, but hosting an industrial software-defined automation controller reinforces the fail-passive gap and localizes it to the SDA-to-balancing-policy interface.

items.title: Biconvex Optimization for Smooth Minimum-Time Trajectories around Convex Obstacles
items.summary: Biconvex optimization is presented for minimum-time motion planning around convex obstacles, ensuring convergence and supporting derivative constraints to arbitrary order. The method jointly convexifies the objective and constraints through a change of variables, handling collision avoidance via time-varying separating planes. The approach reliably produces high-quality trajectories with computation times comparable to state-of-the-art decomposition-based motion planners in drone navigation and dual-arm bin unloading experiments.

items.title: Control Barrier Functions via Minkowski Operations for Safe Navigation among Polytopes
items.summary: Researchers have proposed a method to control barrier functions via Minkowski operations for safe navigation among polytopes in robotics. The approach computes an exact Signed Distance Function (SDF) using companion convex programs and leverages geometric properties of 2D Minkowski operations to derive a unified analytical expression for the gradient of the SDF.

items.title: Contact-Driven Localization in a Freeform Robotic Self-Assembled Structure
items.summary: Researchers Mohammadali Rashidioun, Michael Sosa, and Petras Swissler propose a novel contact-driven localization method for modular robots that uses local communication through binary contact information to form diverse structures. The method leverages a virtual-force framework where robots attract toward dock-connected neighbors and repel from non-connected ones, requiring minimal onboard sensing and no external infrastructure. Simulations show effective localization during the assembly of towers and cantilevers, enabling accurate, scalable, and free-form self-assembly.
